Lutris Advanced Configuration Options - an Overview

While installing your game with Lutris, you will no doubt have noticed some additional configuration options. This section will give a brief overview of them and what they do.

Note: This list is subject to change as features are added/removed in future Lutris releases.

Runner Options

x360ce dinput 8 mode

This option enables the old direct input method of controller recognition from DirectX8 for use with the x360ce program (a Windows utility for connecting and managing XBox 360 controllers). Some older games will require this to be able to correctly recognise and utilize a connected controller.

This should be used only if the builtin Wine xinput implementation has failed to correctly recognise/map your controller.

x360ce xinput 9.1.0 mode

This configures the x360ce program to utilize the more modern xinput method which shipped with Windows Vista and later Windows Operating Systems. Some newer games based on DirectX9 and above will require this mode to be enabled to correctly interface with attached controllers.

This should be used only if the builtin Wine xinput implementation has failed to correctly recognise/map your controller.

Use dumbxinput Emulator

Uses the DLLs provided by the dumbxinput emulator project.

Note: No matter which xinput connection method you are using, you must make sure the Xinput Architecture is set to the correct value for the type of application you are attempting to run. 32-bit for 32-bit applications and so on.

Mouse Warp Override

Some games have issues controller the mouse. This option provides three settings to help address this.

  • Enabled - default behaviour. Mouse pointer warped only when exclusively required by the application.
  • Force - always warp the mouse pointer, regardless of need.
  • Disabled - never warp the mouse pointer.

Offscreen Rendering Mode

Avoids the depth buffer copy between offscreen and onscreen targets. Introduces fallbacks in some drivers and exposes bugs in others.

You can usually leave this as the default value.

Strict Draw Ordering

This ensures any pending drawing operations are sent to the driver, even if such a delay would impact performance. Best to leave disabled, unless absolutely required.

Use GLSL

Enable OpenGL's shader language. Recommend leaving this on. Vulkan drivers have their own compiler (SPIR-V), but there is no harm in leaving GLSL on regardless. If the application does not require it, it will not make use of it.

Render Target Lock Mode

Select which mode is used to render on-screen targets. You can usually leave this as the default value, unless a guide specifies using a different setting.

Use XVidMode to Switch Resolutions

If your application requires a different resolution in order to run, you can allow Wine to use the XVidMode extension in order to achieve this more easily.

System Options

Run in a terminal

If your game is crashing, enabling this option will launch a terminal session and attempt to run the application from within that session. This is useful for debugging, as it can often lead to error/crash messages being made available and providing much needed hints about why the game is failing to run.

Command Prefix & Include/Exclude Process

Here you can specify additional commands to be executed in front of the game's execution command. Include and Exclude processes is used to modify the default process monitoring lists (how Lutris knows when a game has crashed/exited). For example, if there is a setup program which runs prior to starting the main executable, you would want to exclude that setup program from process monitoring, otherwise, when it closes to launch the main application, Lutris may interpret this as the game having quit and terminate the wineserver process.

Restrict to Single Core

Pretty straightforward: prevent the game's process from utilizing more than 1 core. Sometimes required for older applications that cannot function properly on a multi-core/threaded system.

Disable Lutris Runtime

The Lutris Runtime is experimental and is best left disabled, which is the default behaviour for now. It introduces some additional libraries when Enabled to attempt to provide better compatibility and uniformity across different Linux Distributions running Lutris.

Disable Process Monitor

With this setting enabled, Lutris will not know when a running game has quit. Useful if you want to eliminate Lutris as a possible cause for why an application keeps exiting.

Rest Pulseaudio

Restarts the Pulseaudio daemon before launching the game.

Reduce Pulseaudio Latency

Often required to fix missing or garbled sound in games.

Killswitch File

This setting can be used to provide a path to a file which, upon deletion, causing Lutris to terminate the running of the game. For example, when /dev/input/sr0 disappears after unplugging a joystick.

xboxdrv config

If using the xboxdrv package, you can specify the path to the config file you have generated in this section. It will be greyed out if no xboxdrv package has been detected as installed.

SDL2 Gamepad Mapping

SDL is a cross-platform software library for multimedia hardware support. SDL2 is the current version of the software and is in use by most modern games as a means of interfacing with a controller and other gaming peripherals. Here you can specify a custom SDL2 button mapping config for your controller(s).

Use Xephyr

Xephyr is a display server and is used to provide better compatibility for older games requiring 8BPP or 16BPP (bits per pixel) colour modes.
